parts.name: key body

physics.Basic_description: A row of rectangular white plastic levers arranged horizontally along the front bottom edge of the chassis.
physics.Functional_description: Primary input interface for playing notes; pressing them triggers sound generation.
physics.Grasped_description: Not suitable for grasping the object; individual keys are small, movable, and fragile under lateral load.
physics.reason: Standard piano keys are thin-walled hollow shells to reduce inertia and material cost.

physics.Basic_description: Tiny yellow rectangular caps attached to slider mechanisms on the control panel.
physics.Functional_description: Provide a grip surface for the user to slide potentiometers up and down to adjust parameters.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small and delicate for robotic grasping; manipulating them requires fine tip interaction.
physics.reason: Small molded components are effectively solid or thick-walled relative to their size.

collisionFilter.description: Self-contact excluded between directly connected rigid groups, including the fixed base; nonadjacent contacts retained

simulation.inertia: Source URDF link inertials; missing inertials use geometry-derived defaults (density 1000 kg/m³)
simulation.friction: Source URDF mu1 as sliding friction; torsional 0.005, rolling 0.0001
simulation.contact: MuJoCo soft contacts (solref 0.01 1); source restitution is displayed, not converted
simulation.material: Rigid bodies; Young’s modulus and Poisson ratio are annotations, not soft-body parameters

interaction.description: Switchable virtual joint damping and reflected armature for interactive inspection; source properties are unchanged.
interaction.rule: damping ≥ rated effort / rated speed; armature = 2% child subtree mass (slide) or 2% mass × collision radius² (hinge)
